top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, KLOwen, Lightforce, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, herbst expanders, o rings, SLB, Aliwell, Virtualcare, DM Insights
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, rentability, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, adaptive aligner change, efficiency in second and third order movements, average visit reduction, decrease of emergencies, dynamic scheduling, practice optimisation, staff efficiency, staff satisfaction
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or chair time. Some believe the workflow changes are not worth the effort, or that the ROI is unclear, especially for braces. Others question whether these efficiency claims apply to their specific practice setup or bracket system.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Show how braces saves appointments, time and money
Reduced chair time, recent studies, practice efficiencies for aligners
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct, head-to-head studies quantifying ROI and efficiency for specific appliances (e.g., Damon, Spark, Lightforce) and in diverse geographies are limited. More granular, practice-level economic analyses and real-world workflow case studies are needed.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, comparison to intraoral scan, FDA class I, occlusal assessment, accuracy of AI detecting malocclusions, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, accuracy of scanning, ALIGNER UNSEAT TRACKING
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human orthodontist, especially for detecting clinical changes or making diagnostic decisions. Some express distrust or fear of AI, or specifically doubt the reliability of SmartSTL for monitoring or refinement.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, clinical study, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more peer-reviewed, quantitative studies directly comparing DM’s AI and SmartSTL outputs to gold-standard clinical assessments, especially for specific diagnostic tasks and across diverse patient populations.
